channel.title: matterunknown
channel.description: Ryan Silver's independent research lab. Serious work on identity — especially the identity of AI agents — and niche projects built for the joy of it.

item.title: The Credential Remembers Who. Nothing Remembers Why.
item.description: Intent tokens as the missing identity layer for AI agents — built on existing standards, attesting to why an agent acts, not just who it is.

item.title: The Workload Is the Reasoning Session
item.description: Why agentic identity breaks the identity stack's assumptions, and what an attestation layer for reasoning sessions would look like.

item.title: The Card Market Has a Data Problem
item.description: Pokémon cards as an alternative asset class with a pricing-data problem worth modeling.

item.title: Vibe Coding with My 10 Year Old
item.description: Building a Roblox farming game with my son over three weekends.

item.title: Identity Is a Tattoo. Design It Like One.
item.description: Identity architecture is permanent design. Treat it with tattoo-level regret aversion.

item.title: Can an AI Agent Have a Verifiable Identity?
item.description: A running lab where AI agents register, attest, and are cryptographically governed.

item.title: The Agent Identity Gap
item.description: We can authenticate agents. We have no framework for authorizing intent.

item.title: Synthetic Identity Is Already Here. We Just Call It Fraud.
item.description: Synthetic identity fraud is an identity-system failure, not a crime story.

item.title: When Your Identity Outlives You
item.description: Digital identity after death, and the gap between death and deletion.

item.title: Why We Built a Council
item.description: Why a council of disagreeing models beats one confident model.

item.title: The Cheat Code That Isn't
item.description: AI sales gurus, shortcut culture, and the system selling you the system.

item.title: The NHI Problem Is a Human Problem
item.description: Non-human identities are dangerous for very human reasons.

item.title: What Break Glass Access Reveals About Trust
item.description: Emergency access procedures are a confession of what organizations actually trust.

item.title: Building a Demo Environment That Lies Convincingly
item.description: Building a security demo environment that lies convincingly — and what that teaches about manufactured trust.

item.title: AI Agents Don't Have Identity. That's the Problem.
item.description: AI agents have access but no meaningful identity of their own.

item.title: On Writing a Character Who Doesn't Know Who She Is
item.description: Narrative identity, from the craft side.

item.title: The Shared Account Is a Moral Problem, Not a Technical One
item.description: Shared accounts as an accountability problem before a technical one.
